hook_text: R1 248 plus R397 at the till. Beat the cashier with one round number and one tiny fix.
clip_script: Supermarket in East London. R1 248 plus R397. Do not reach for columns. 397 is three short of 400. Add 400: 1 648. Take the 3 back: 1 645. Done before the receipt prints. Now the bus: 2 650 kilometres total, 1 875 driven, how far to go? Round 1 875 to 1 900. 2 650 minus 1 900 is 750. But you took away 25 too many, so give it back: 775. Say the fix out loud and you will never get the direction wrong. Now check the other way: 1 875 plus 775. 1 875 plus 25 is 1 900, plus 750 is 2 650. True. Estimate, round and fix, then check the other way round. Two tricks on every sum, and nothing slips past.
visual_style: Whiteboard empty number line with jumps drawn live; a 397 morphing into 400 with a small minus 3 tag; a till receipt and a bus odometer.
pacing: The till sum in one breath, the bus subtraction with the direction fix, then the inverse check and the rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and do your next shopping total in your head before the till does.
